body.estimand_functional: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and let \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  No independently derived repaired lower and upper maps have yet been proved equivalent.  The complete all-regime frontier, its unresolved transition logarithms, and the necessary direction of the known-propensity comparison therefore remain open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

sampling_model.design: Project-specific strengthening: \(X\) is known to be exactly uniform on the entire cube \([0,1]^d\), not merely to have a bounded density or to be uniform on a support with holes.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary.  The pointwise boxes \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) are project-specific fixed interior regression margins on the canonical continuous representatives.
sampling_model.overlap: The project-specific numerical overlap box is \(e(x)\in[1/4,3/4]\) for every \(x\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate in a larger model with a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes; Section 3.1 supplies localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger machinery.  Its binary lower submodel uses a density uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\), so that lower bound does not transfer downward to the present exact full-cube uniform-design subclass.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.

Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioner under total-variation smoothness, a different null manifold and separation metric from constant CATE.

Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions, rather than a fixed-sample three-smoothness CATE radius.

Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimation of a signed expected conditional covariance functional; they guide nuisance resolution but do not test an unknown constant CATE.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: The established all-regime observational bracket and matched no-penalty region remain valid, and the rough stress point now has a sharper original-class converse.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the general lower bound is \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit upper bound is \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), conditioning on macro signs and normalizing by the exact common one-observation law proves \(c n^{-3/10}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19}\), hence \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{1/10}\).  The matching upper route remains open because a legal covariance-masking alternative makes all proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population means vanish.  No common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests and adjacent minimax results do not give a fixed-sample sharp radius on this project-specific binary exact-uniform class.  The direct-Hellinger calculation now proves a material \(n^{-3/10}\) lower bound at the canonical rough tuple, but the best proved upper exponent there is \(4/19\), and the complete three-index map and its transition logarithms remain unknown.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction between a constant-effect composite null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and collision information beyond binned covariance means.  The sign-dependent common marginal is sufficient for a sharp new converse at one rough tuple, while the exact masking example shows that an attaining test must use an omnibus signal richer than products of within-bin covariance contrasts.
project_justification.fill: The paper currently supplies the explicit total fourth-order test and all-regime bracket, the known-propensity benchmark and no-penalty region, a corrected constant-null-supported nested construction, and a direct fixed-\(n\) Hellinger converse of order \(n^{-3/10}\) at \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\).  It also gives an explicit legal blind alternative that rules out the proposed pair-factor upper dichotomy.  These are field-level advances and precise constraints on the missing matched frontier, not a claim that the frontier is complete.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class.  Its Theorem 1 concerns pointwise CATE estimation in a larger model, and its binary lower submodel uses a covariate density uniform on a support with holes.  Here only its Section 3.2 partition-mixture Hellinger lemma is instantiated after separately proving exact full-cube cell masses, common predictive marginals, and density-ratio bounds.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 supplies collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing on a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024 supplies projected-covariance validity and spline power under its own common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026 gives asymptotic homogeneity procedures under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026 derives separate resolutions for a signed expected conditional-covariance estimation functional.  None supplies the new constant-null-supported \(n^{-3/10}\) fixed-sample converse or repairs the covariance-masking failure of the proposed upper statistic on this identical class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected bounded-overlap construction satisfies the original margins through \(|u|\leq C_bq_e\) and \(|v|\leq C_bq_b\).  Conditional on macro signs, its common singleton likelihood lies between \(11/12\) and \(13/12\) relative to the interior reference.  The localized Hellinger calculation has \(\delta_1,\delta_2=O(\delta)\), \(\delta_3=0\), and cost \(Cn^2h\delta^2\); at \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), this is \(O(\epsilon^7n^{-1/10})\) and is eventually absorbed by \(n^3hH\delta^4=\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\).  Hellinger convexity adds no outer-sign term.  The fixed-reference fifth projection still diverges and remains a valid warning against that chi-square normalization, but it is not an obstruction to the common-marginal comparison.  The unresolved obstruction is now upper-side: a legal alternative can have nonconstant CATE and \(g_B(c)=0\) in every fine bin, annihilating the proposed pair-factor population signals.  A richer statistic, all sparse-regime concentration bounds, and all-regime matching are still missing.
body.honest_scope: The statistical class remains the original binary exact-full-cube-uniform Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins; no nuisance-rate or estimator-side condition has been inserted.  The proved global result is still a bracket, augmented by a sharper \(n^{-3/10}\) lower bound and a strict known-versus-unknown separation at one rough tuple.  The no-penalty subregion remains sufficient but not necessary.  The complete frontier, the exact propensity-equality region, and unproved transition logarithms remain open.  The corrected third and fifth projections diagnose one construction, while the masking proposition diagnoses one proposed upper architecture; neither is promoted to a universal impossibility theorem.
body.interpretation: At the rough stress tuple, unknown assignment is provably consequential: the observational critical radius is at least order \(n^{-3/10}\), whereas supplying the propensity permits order \(n^{-2/5}\), so their ratio diverges at least as \(n^{1/10}\).  This is a detectability statement about worst-case laws, not a guarantee for any fitted forest, and non-rejection cannot be interpreted as evidence of homogeneous effects.
